name: @cytoscape-web/app-runtime
description: Build-time SDK for Cytoscape Web apps: one call configures Module Federation correctly.
//repository: REQUIRED for provenance, not decoration. npm validates that this
matches the repository the sigstore bundle attests to; an absent or
mismatched url fails the publish with a 422 — and `npm publish
--dry-run` cannot catch it, because a dry run never contacts the
registry and so never runs that validation.
//publishConfig: A scoped package defaults to RESTRICTED. Without this the publish either
fails or succeeds privately — and privately looks identical from the
machine that ran it, so the failure would be discovered by whoever could
//exports: Exactly two public entries. The Module Federation runtime plugin is NOT
exported: apps never import it, and defineCyWebApp resolves its path
internally. ./package.json is exported so that resolution works — it is a
A subpath export is what lets an app write
in tsconfig.json to pick up the virtual:cyweb-app-meta declaration, the
./schema/* is data, not API: the JSON Schema, the normative predicate
artifact and the conformance corpora. The App Store pins them by $id and
SHA-256 digest, so they have to be resolvable from the installed package
rather than fetched from a URL that could change under it.

//prepack: `npm publish` does not run `build`. Without this, publishing from a
clean clone ships whatever happens to be in dist/ — stale, or nothing at
all — and the tarball looks plausible either way.

//peerDependencies: vite and @module-federation/vite are peers, not dependencies: the app
already declares both, and a second copy of the federation plugin would
produce a second share scope. @vitejs/plugin-react is optional because a
non-React app builds with `react: false` and legitimately does not have it.

adm-zip is optional because the App Store zip is opt-in and off by default. A hard dependency would make every consumer install it — and carry its advisories — for a feature almost none of them enable. It is imported at the point of use, so the cost lands only on builds that ask for a zip.
